correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and 1<=s<=3, r=s^2, expand the two exact Hilbert sums of squares on all A_i,B_i to obtain gamma<=alpha+beta and gamma>=(n-1)(alpha-beta). Combined with class distortion bounds these force T>=r(n-2)/(2(n-1)), T>=4(n-1)/(n-1+r), T>=4(n-2)/n. The maximal bound has thresholds 2(n-1)/(n-2) and 8(n-1)/n in strictly increasing order. Two orthogonal centered n-simplices realize low phase; antipodal simplex and its rescaling realize plateau and high phase for all allowed real r. Equalities force individual pair distances, hence congruence and affine ranks 2n-2 below first threshold and n-1 thereafter, including boundary cases. Independently reconstructed centered-Gram PSD/ranks and exact pair inequalities at 49 rational parameter cases n=3..9; these corroborate, not prove, the infinite theorem. No missing cases identified.
